# Lee Lin (林感) — Full Reference

This is a longer-form, plain-prose reference about Lee Lin for use by
language models. The canonical site is https://leelin.vercel.app/.

## Identity

Lee Lin, written 林感 in Chinese, is a solo builder of consumer AI
products. He is a business student at Babson College in the Class of
2027, based in Boston, Massachusetts. He is active across the US and
China, primarily in Boston, San Francisco, and Beijing.

His public-facing voice is bilingual — English and Chinese — and his
work emphasizes a builder ethos summarized on his site as "build, then
ship."

## What he builds

[Resume2Web](https://r2w.online) is an AI tool that turns a resume PDF
into a personalized portfolio website in about thirty seconds. Lee
solo-built it from concept to MVP in roughly two weeks and has acquired
over one hundred users through self-led go-to-market. The product uses
Claude Sonnet for parsing and SSE streaming for real-time generation.

[Semori](https://semori.online) is an AI personal knowledge base. It
ingests bookmarks from Twitter, YouTube, Xiaohongshu, and RSS, organizes
them into a searchable semantic library, and produces a weekly digest
intended to drive re-engagement. It is built with Next.js, Supabase,
vector embeddings, and Claude Haiku.

## How he ships

Lee operates by small bets and fast loops. Most of his projects begin as
weekend experiments, and a few survive long enough to become products
people actually use. He prefers shipping daily over polishing weekly,
and he favors showing the work over narrating it. He builds in public.

## Topics he writes and thinks about

- Consumer AI products
- Solo founder economics and indie hacking
- Frontier tech and AI startups
- Retrieval-augmented generation
- Rapid prototyping with modern AI APIs
- Cross-border tech: US and China product strategy
- Growth marketing for early-stage products

## Off-screen

Lee climbs in the high mountains, including ice climbing on frozen
waterfalls. He drinks too much coffee and plays badminton.

## Site

The personal site at https://leelin.vercel.app/ is built with Next.js,
Tailwind CSS, and Motion (Framer Motion). The visual language is a
"chapter-book" aesthetic: warm cream paper, Cormorant Garamond serif
display type, Caveat handwritten accents, JetBrains Mono labels, and an
all-black palette. The voice is part journal, part zine. Page hash
sections are #about, #work, #hobby, and #contact.
